cases.case: Jaya Thakur v. Union of India (challenge to the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023)
cases.issue: Whether Sections 6 and 7 of the 2023 Act, which removed the Chief Justice of India from the panel that selects the CEC and Election Commissioners, compromise the Election Commission's independence.
cases.bench: Justices Dipankar Datta and S.C. Sharma (CJI Surya Kant recused on 20 Mar 2026)
cases.last_event: The two judges split on whether a larger bench was needed, then unanimously sent the papers to the CJI so a Constitution Bench can be constituted. Decision had been reserved on 30 Jul 2026.
cases.next_step: Constitution Bench to be constituted; no hearing date announced. Separately, on 5 Oct 2026 a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana issued notice to the Centre and the ECI on a plea asking whether CEC Gyanesh Kumar can individually exercise powers vested in the full Commission, and said 'Any modification to Form 6 has not been approved by us' (IANS; PTI).

cases.case: State of Uttar Pradesh v. Jai Bir Singh
cases.issue: Whether to revisit the 1978 Bangalore Water Supply test for what counts as an 'industry' under Section 2(j) of the Industrial Disputes Act.
cases.bench: Nine judges led by CJI Surya Kant
cases.last_event: Four judges backed the CJI's narrower 'discernible commercial character' test; four (Nagarathna, Datta, Bhuyan, Bagchi) backed the 1978 test; Justice P.S. Narasimha left the 1978 test undisturbed because the ID Act has been repealed. The 1978 test continues for pending ID Act disputes.
cases.next_step: None in this case. The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 definition is to be read on its own terms.

cases.case: Sabarimala reference (review of the 2018 women's entry judgment and connected religious-freedom questions)
cases.issue: Scope of freedom of religion under Articles 25 and 26, the essential religious practices doctrine and 'constitutional morality'; the reference also covers the Dawoodi Bohra and Parsi women matters.
cases.bench: CJI Surya Kant and Justices B.V. Nagarathna, M.M. Sundresh, Ahsanuddin Amanullah, Aravind Kumar, Augustine George Masih, Prasanna B. Varale, R. Mahadevan and Joymalya Bagchi
cases.last_event: Judgment reserved after 16 days of hearing.
cases.next_step: Verdict. The CJI indicated in August it could come by 6 Oct 2026 (LiveLaw, Kerala Kaumudi); no verdict found as of 11 Oct 2026.

cases.case: N. Ravi v. Speaker, Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly
cases.issue: Whether legislative privilege under Article 194 overrides free speech under Article 19(1)(a); arose from the TN Assembly's 2003 order to arrest editors of The Hindu over an editorial.
cases.bench: CJI Surya Kant and Justices Aravind Kumar, P.K. Mishra, Joymalya Bagchi, Vipul Pancholi, Shree Chandrashekhar and V. Mohana
cases.status_text: Disposed as infructuous; questions of law left open
cases.last_event: Reference closed because the Assembly resolution was withdrawn in 2004.
cases.next_step: None. The legal question awaits a future case.

cases.case: Association for Democratic Reforms v. Election Commission of India and connected SIR petitions
cases.issue: Legality of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar and later phases.
cases.bench: CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi (Bihar ruling)
cases.status_text: Bihar SIR upheld; later-phase challenges pending
cases.last_event: Notice issued on a Delhi petition alleging SIR notices were issued mechanically. In August the Court directed the ECI to disclose pending appeals in West Bengal. Bihar SIR upheld unanimously on 27 May 2026.
cases.next_step: Hearings on Delhi and West Bengal matters; no dates in sources found.

cases.case: NEET-UG 2026 protest FIRs (Jantar Mantar protests of 20 July 2026)
cases.issue: Whether FIRs filed across India against students who protested the NEET-UG paper leak should be quashed.
cases.bench: CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana
cases.status_text: FIRs quashed under Article 142; related matters pending
cases.last_event: On 1 Sep 2026 the Court quashed FIRs for incidents of 20-25 July, barred fresh FIRs except one Delhi Police FIR against 2,873 people with alleged 'serious criminal antecedents', and said the order is not a precedent. On 16 Sep it dismissed as premature a plea to reconstitute the High-Power Enquiry Committee on police excesses (formed 18 Aug).
cases.next_step: The Union must frame a compensation policy, including for families of students who died by suicide, within three months of 1 Sep 2026.

cases.case: States' power to tax minerals: Mineral Area Development Authority v. Steel Authority of India (2024) and the MMDR (Amendment) Act, 2026
cases.issue: Whether Parliament can bar states from taxing mineral rights and mineral-bearing land, after a 2024 nine-judge ruling upheld state taxing powers.
cases.status_text: Challenge to 2026 amendment announced; filing not confirmed
cases.last_event: Karnataka, Kerala and Telangana said they would jointly challenge the MMDR (Amendment) Act, 2026 in the Supreme Court; Congress's Jairam Ramesh said a petition had been prepared.
cases.next_step: Filing of the states' petition; no listing found as of 11 Oct 2026.

cases.case: Arjun Floor Mills v. State of Orissa
cases.issue: Validity of Orissa's additional tax on dealers by annual turnover (10% for ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore, 15% above ₹1 crore); the state argues the 2017 tax changes make the reference academic.
cases.bench: Seven-judge Constitution Bench (members not named in source)
cases.last_event: Judgment reserved after one day of hearing.

cases.case: Challenges to the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Act, 2026
cases.issue: Validity of the 2026 amendment that replaces the definition of a transgender person with listed categories and adds medical board review of identity certificates.
cases.last_event: Union assured the Court of interim validity for existing identity cards. Earlier, the Court declined an interim stay (May) and issued notice on 15 Jun on the Union's plea to transfer High Court challenges to itself.
cases.next_step: Hearing on transfer and merits; no date in sources found.

cases.case: Arjun Gopal v. Union of India (WP(C) 728/2015)
cases.issue: Whether and how firecrackers may be sold and burst in Delhi-NCR, as part of the long-running case on the capital's air pollution.
cases.bench: Justices M M Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale
cases.status_text: Diwali 2026 relaxation ordered; compliance hearing due
cases.last_event: Allowed certified green crackers in Delhi-NCR on 7 and 8 Nov 2026, only from 6 to 7 am and 8 to 10 pm, with sales from 4 to 6 Nov at notified sites (no online sales), QR-coded CSIR-NEERI certified boxes and no-cracker zones within 300 metres of hospitals, schools and silence zones. The year-round ban returns on 9 Nov. CPCB and state boards to file air quality reports for 2 to 6 Nov, the festival days and 9 to 30 Nov.
cases.next_step: Affidavits and reports due by 14 Dec 2026; listed for compliance on 16 Dec 2026.

cases.case: Petitions on alleged theft and misuse of donations to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust (Narendra Kumar Goswami, Ajay Kumar Rai, Sudhakar Singh and Hindu Dharma Parishad)
cases.issue: Whether the alleged theft of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya needed a CBI or court-monitored probe and a forensic audit of the trust's finances.
cases.bench: CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana
cases.status_text: Closed after police chargesheet; CBI probe refused
cases.last_event: Closed the petitions after being told the police had filed a chargesheet against eight accused. Refused to transfer the probe to the CBI and let the Uttar Pradesh police SIT, which now includes a forensic auditor, continue. The SIT found 105 instances of unauthorised removal of cash. Petitioners may assist the trial court as victims are allowed to.
cases.next_step: Trial in the trial court; the SIT may file further reports there as its forensic audit continues.

cases.case: Democratic Medical Association v. National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (heard with FAIMA and United Doctors Front petitions on entrance exams)
cases.issue: Whether NBEMS must give each NEET-PG candidate the question paper, OMR sheet and answer key after the exam, instead of question IDs only.
cases.bench: Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe
cases.status_text: NBEMS told to file written submissions
cases.last_event: Asked NBEMS why NEET-PG questions should not be disclosed after the exam ('What happens to transparency?'). NBEMS argued its question bank is small and a national asset. The court directed NBEMS to file written submissions on how disclosure could compromise the exam. Notice in the petition was issued on 15 Oct 2026.
cases.next_step: Written submissions by NBEMS; no next date reported.
